note: Content corrections raised by the 2026-09-08 Codex audit. Claude proposes a corrected version; only the named reviewer may resolve it, and a resolved record alone never restores the defective content: the replacement must be installed at the recorded toVersion or the item stays withheld. A withheld item is kept out of lessons and assessments and the manifest reports the reduced coverage rather than hiding it.

corrections.reason: The explanation called "Falling rocks." a complete statement. It is a fragment that is conventional on a sign. Teaching it as complete contradicts SE.complete, which this pilot also assesses.
corrections.correctedExplanation: Signs often use short fragments. "Danger!" is an exclamation and "Falling rocks." names a thing without telling us what it does, so it is a fragment, not a complete sentence. Both are capitalized and take end marks, and a sign is one of the few places a fragment is the right choice. In your own writing, a complete sentence needs a subject and a verb.
correctedCommonErrors: Calling any capitalized group of words with a period a complete sentence.
Copying sign style into ordinary writing, where a fragment is usually an error.
corrections.resolution: Parent approved the corrected sign explanation on 2026-09-09 and directed that the transfer task be restored. Installed as version 2 of c0.pu.capitals-endmarks.19.

corrections.reason: The explanation described watch as using "the short a sound". In ordinary Canadian English the vowel in watch is not the short a of cat, so the description misdescribes the pronunciation and undercuts the phonics teaching. The parent supplied the final wording, which avoids naming a phonics category for the vowel at all.
corrections.correctedExplanation: Watch ends in tch. The spelling tch often appears at the end of a short one-syllable word after a vowel. The vowel in watch sounds like the vowel in wash for many Canadian speakers, so do not describe it as the short a in cat. Watch is a common spelling to learn and remember.
correctedCommonErrors: Assuming the letter a always spells the vowel of cat.
Writing wach or wotch by matching the letter instead of the sound.
corrections.resolution: Parent approved a simplified explanation on 2026-09-09 and supplied the wording. Installed verbatim as version 2 of c0.sp.patterns.06.

corrections.reason: The editing prompt asked for exactly four corrections but its intended repair was ambiguous: with the plural pronoun they, the verb are is correct, while a past-tense reading needs were. Without a stated intended meaning a reviewer cannot count the targets consistently.
corrections.intendedMeaning: Mia, one person, checks two labels in the present; the labels differ from each other.
answerKey: Capitalize the first word: mia becomes Mia.
Subject-verb agreement: check becomes checks, because Mia is singular.
Pronoun: her becomes they, referring to the two labels.
corrections.notAccepted: Changing are to were. The intended meaning is present tense, and they are is already correct with the plural antecedent. A past-tense rewrite changes the meaning rather than repairing an error.
corrections.resolution: Parent approved the explicit key for Form A on 2026-09-09. Installed as version 2 of c0.assessment.a.33: the prompt now states the intended meaning, and the rubric carries the model answer, the four named targets, and what is not accepted.

corrections.reason: The Form B editing prompt names four targets but has no stated intended meaning or explicit key, so it shares the Form A ambiguity.
corrections.intendedMeaning: Yesterday the group inspected one teacher's folder carefully.
answerKey: Capitalize the first word: yesterday becomes Yesterday.
Verb tense: inspect becomes inspected, because yesterday sets the past.
Possessive apostrophe: teachers becomes teacher's, one teacher owning the folder.
corrections.notAccepted: Reading teachers as plural and writing teachers'. The intended meaning names one teacher; a reviewer records a plural reading as a reasonable alternative for review rather than a correct or incorrect answer.
corrections.resolution: Parent approved the explicit key for Form B on 2026-09-09. Installed as version 2 of c0.assessment.b.33: the prompt now states the intended meaning, and the rubric carries the model answer, the four named targets, and what is not accepted.
